photo.viewpoint: Viewing the Palace of Westminster from near the south bank of the River Thames
photo.hero_placement: Big Ben / Elizabeth Tower sits right of the visual center, the full tower clearly visible from its base to the spire tip, uncropped, with strictly true architectural proportions
photo.skyline: The Palace of Westminster stretches horizontally beside Big Ben, forming the classic London skyline; the buildings use real warm beige stone, with soft golden highlights where the setting sun strikes
photo.river: The broad River Thames fills the foreground, occupying about 20-25% of the photography area; the water is low-saturation blue-gray with fine natural ripples and slight building reflections
photo.scale_reference: A single very small London tour boat may appear as a scale reference, but must not steal the subject
photo.background: Modern London buildings may appear faintly in the distance, but must be de-emphasized
photo.time: London evening, golden hour transitioning into blue hour
photo.sky_gradient: a natural gradient from pale gray-blue to soft misty violet to light peach pink to faint warm gold
photo.clouds: A few characteristically British stratus layers and soft cumulus, a slightly overcast feel, but never gloomy
photo.rim_light: Sunlight passes through the clouds from behind the side, tracing a delicate golden rim light along Big Ben's edges
photo.lens: 50-85mm architectural photography, medium-telephoto compression, building verticals kept perfectly straight, no fisheye, no exaggerated wide-angle distortion
photo.quality: authentic London travel photography, premium architectural photography, cinematic golden hour, real stone texture, natural HDR, high dynamic range, 4K

vector.hero_simplification: Simplify the complex Gothic structure into rectangles + thin vertical lines + triangles + pointed arches + ultra-fine geometric lines; render each clock face as a single restrained pale-gold circle; no thick black outlines
vector.supporting: A simplified Palace of Westminster extends horizontally to the left of Big Ben; the complex Gothic facade is highly geometricized, keeping only the row of spires, the rectangular main body, the towers, the pointed-arch windows, and the horizontal base; the building must be clearly lower than Big Ben
vector.sun: A huge translucent geometric circle sun sits behind and slightly left of Big Ben, in very soft British mist pink / Dusty Rose / Pale Peach; the circle is partially occluded by Big Ben and the Palace; no realistic sun texture
vector.river: A single ultra-fine deep gray-blue horizontal line beneath the buildings sets the baseline, with 5-7 ultra-thin horizontal lines of varying lengths below it in mist blue, gray-blue, and light navy, abstracting the Thames water surface
vector.easter_egg: Optionally hide one tiny minimalist red London double-decker bus silhouette as an easter egg, no larger than 1% of the frame
vector.feel: Keep the feel of an architectural design archive; never drift into tourist cartoon illustration
